children.label: In behavioural science, “positive” means something is added, not that it is morally good. Positive reinforcement means adding a valued consequence after a behaviour. Over time, that behaviour tends to appear more often in similar situations. It is different from negative reinforcement, which involves removing something to change behaviour.

Over time, that behaviour tends to appear more often in similar situations. It is different from negative reinforcement, which involves removing something to change behaviour.
